narrative:
The model estimates a 67% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that stood out compared to employees the system expected to stay.

The strongest influence was that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is a major signal the model associates with higher turnover risk, as it suggests you have viable alternatives that could pull you away.

Next, your relatively short overall career experience of 1-5 years pushed the prediction in the opposite direction. Most employees the model predicted would stay also had limited experience, so this factor actually worked in your favor and reduced the likelihood of leaving. However, it was not enough to outweigh the other signals.

The third important factor was your employment in the “other” sector. This category, which includes 22% of employees predicted to stay, still contributed toward a higher chance of departure in your specific case, likely because it lacks some stabilizing characteristics found in sectors like medical or education.

Taken together, the combination of external opportunities and sector-specific dynamics created enough concern about potential departure that the system could not confidently support a promotion at this time.

You and your manager should discuss ways to strengthen your connection to the organization, such as exploring internal growth paths or addressing any unmet needs, to reduce the risk of leaving in the future. (248 words)
